expert_synthesis.chemistry_takeaways: The measured m167 curve shows a strong ratio response, especially in V2. m147 is comparatively stable, so condition response is molecule specific. m125 shows large coupled condition and loading variation. Polar and aza chemotypes produce heterogeneous errors with no universal signed correction.
expert_synthesis.ml_takeaways: Observed errors now favor learning local molecule by condition interactions and high volume tail behavior. Large errors occur in both directions. Loading effects are promising but confounded. The endpoint ordering anomaly hypothesis is unsupported.
agreements: Matched condition curves remain more informative than isolated novelty.
Tail and sparse chemotype measurements are valuable when tied to a competing explanation.
V2 deserves extra attention because ratio and tail errors are often larger than V1 errors.
disagreements: Chemistry priors favor broad silica interaction coverage, while the ML evidence argues against a universal polar group correction.
The previous endpoint anomaly rationale is contradicted by the measured m13 and m80 labels and their recorded predictions.
expert_synthesis.planner_resolution: Concentrate the new batch on an expanded m167 ratio/load curve, matched m125 contrasts, local contrasts around the m160/m161/m216 and m90 regimes, and a smaller set of orthogonal sparse chemotypes. Deprioritize further endpoint-order diagnostics and broad m147 replication.

batch_strategy: Use four linked groups: m167 ratio and loading contrasts; m125 condition/load contrasts; local error curves for m160, m161, m216, m90, and m105; and chemically distinct tail or silica-interaction probes. The batch uses observed residuals to choose interpretable contrasts, while retaining several broader probes for Row-distribution coverage.

choices.reason: m167 at 10/1 and 50 microlitres extends the measured ratio curve to a lower load and separates ratio from amount effects.
m167 at 20/1 and 100 microlitres tests whether the strong V2 ratio response persists at an intermediate load.
m167 at 50/1 and 50 microlitres probes continuation or saturation of the observed V2 response at low loading.
m167 at 50/1 and 150 microlitres provides a matched high-load contrast to the low-load extreme.
m125 at 5/1 and 150 microlitres is the key matched extension of the observed m125 load and ratio variation.
m125 at 2/1 and 100 microlitres with a different loading-solvent volume separates the measured 2/1 load contrast further.
m125 at 1/1 and 50 microlitres supplies a low-load anchor for the unusually variable m125 response surface.
m125 at 0/1 and 100 microlitres tests whether its high-volume behavior begins before the measured 1/1 to 5/1 range.
m160 at 2/1 and 150 microlitres tests whether the large measured 5/1 underprediction persists at weaker eluent strength.
m160 at 2/1 and 50 microlitres adds a load contrast to the same basic nitrile chemotype.
m160 at 0/1 and 150 microlitres anchors its condition response below the measured high-error case.
m161 at 5/1 and 100 microlitres tests whether its more accurate measured behavior continues across ratio.
m161 at 0/1 and 150 microlitres provides a weaker-ratio contrast to the measured 2/1 case and the new 5/1 case.
m216 at 2/1 and 50 microlitres tests whether the large 10/1 underprediction is a broad aza-aromatic issue or condition specific.
m216 at 5/1 and 100 microlitres adds an intermediate ratio and load contrast to the measured extreme.
m216 at 1/1 and 150 microlitres probes the lower-ratio, higher-load side of its local response surface.
m90 at 5/1 and 50 microlitres is a direct loading contrast to the measured 150 microlitre m90 tail point.
m90 at 10/1 and 150 microlitres tests whether its measured overprediction at 5/1 changes sign or magnitude at stronger ratio.
m105 at 2/1 and 100 microlitres fills a condition/load gap around the measured 1/1 and 10/1 records.
m105 at 1/1 and 50 microlitres tests whether its modest observed loading sensitivity extends to a smaller injection.
m105 at 0/1 and 50 microlitres supplies a weak-ratio, low-load anchor for its response curve.
m92 at 10/1 and 50 microlitres expands the now measured EA series while isolating loading amount at a common ratio.
m92 at 50/1 and 100 microlitres tests the EA tail under stronger ratio and provides Row coverage beyond the measured central range.
m199 supplies a sulfone-containing acceptor-rich contrast for sparse silica-interaction behavior under DCM.
m211 adds a distinct aza-biaryl case at 5/1 DCM to test whether aza-aromatic tail behavior generalizes beyond m216.
m212 is an amine-containing aromatic probe with a predicted high-volume response, complementary to the nitrile amines.
m208 provides a donor-rich, heavy-atom contrast at 2/1 DCM with unusual loading-solvent volume.
m193 at 0/1 and high loading-solvent volume tests whether the measured nitrobenzaldehyde tail miss persists at weak ratio.
m193 at 2/1 and lower amount supplies a matched condition contrast to the measured 20/1 tail point.
m11 at 1/1 tests whether the large overprediction at 10/1 is ratio dependent in the oxime-like chemotype.
m11 at 2/1 and 50 microlitres gives a lower-load, intermediate-ratio contrast to the measured high-error point.
m146 probes a high predicted endpoint regime at 10/1 DCM against its measured 1/1 aza-aromatic baseline.

hypotheses.content: For m167, PE/EA ratio produces a reproducible, molecule-specific response in which V2 changes more strongly than V1; loading amount may modify the curve.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This is a well-supported condition-response structure that can improve interpolation and V2 tail calibration.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the remaining m167 ratios and loads preserve the observed V2-dominant progression and reveal a separable loading effect?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount and loading-solvent conditions can alter endpoints, but their effects remain confounded with mobile phase and molecule-specific response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Direct load contrasts may reduce systematic interpolation error, especially for V2, but require matched measurements to avoid learning spurious global effects.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed molecule and ratio, do the new m125, m90, m105, and m92 contrasts show coherent amount or loading-solvent shifts?

hypotheses.content: Sparse polar, donor-rich, basic, and aza-aromatic chemotypes contain important local model errors, but the error sign and magnitude are structure and condition specific.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local interaction features or residual modeling may improve tail accuracy without imposing an incorrect universal polar-group correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do additional condition curves for m160, m161, m216, m193, m11, and related aza or amine structures cluster by chemotype or remain heterogeneous?

hypotheses.content: The prior endpoint-order anomaly premise is unsupported: the measured diagnostic compounds have V2 greater than V1, as do the recorded predictions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Further selections should not spend capacity on a presumed ordering defect; joint endpoint modeling should be motivated by residual structure instead.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do any future measured records violate physical endpoint ordering after verified row alignment?

hypotheses.content: m125 occupies a difficult molecule-by-condition regime with large V1/V2 variation and load-linked tail behavior, requiring local response coverage.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Its absolute endpoint errors can materially affect Row-distribution accuracy, and matched measurements can distinguish local response from general tail bias.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed m125 loading amount and loading-solvent volume, how does the remaining ratio curve compare with the observed 1/1, 2/1, and 5/1 records?

hypotheses.content: m147 is a stable low-tail anchor whose shallow measured ratio response shows that strong V2 ratio effects are not universal across molecules.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This prevents overgeneralizing the m167 response and helps the model distinguish molecule-specific condition sensitivity.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do other nonpolar aliphatic aromatics show m147-like shallow response rather than m167-like V2 amplification?

batch_rationale: The previous batch successfully established a V2-dominant m167 ratio response and showed that m147 is comparatively shallow, so the new plan reallocates condition-curve capacity toward m167 and away from m147. Measured m125 records revealed large coupled condition and loading variation, making matched m125 probes more valuable. The large residuals for m160 and m216 support local sparse-chemotype coverage, but opposite signed errors in m11, m90, m161, and m125 reject a universal polar correction. The two endpoint diagnostics measured in normal order, so H4 is rejected and no new endpoint-anomaly selections are made.
expected_learning_value: Highest value is expected from the four m167 contrasts and four m125 contrasts because they directly resolve the strongest observed response structures. The m160/m161/m216 and m90 curves test whether large tail residuals persist across conditions. m105 and m92 improve condition coverage with measured anchors. The remaining sulfone, aza, amine, donor, nitro, oxime, and high-endpoint probes broaden local generalization while preserving interpretable chemical questions.
feedback_interpretation: Previous real feedback supports H1 strongly, supports a local m125 interaction hypothesis, and supports H3 only as a heterogeneous local-error concern. It weakens the earlier universal nonlinear-condition claim because m147 is shallow. It leaves H2 unresolved because m125 load contrasts are confounded. It rejects H4 because both m13 and m80 measured endpoints obey V2 greater than V1 and their recorded predictions are ordered. The new batch therefore tests revised, molecule-specific response hypotheses rather than repeating the prior broad narrative.
